t: Section 501(b) of title 46, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:“(b) By Head of Agency.—When the head of an agency responsible for the administration of the navigation or vessel-inspection laws considers it necessary in the interest of national defense, the individual, following a determination by the Maritime Administrator, acting in the Administrator’s capacity as Director, National Shipping Authority, of the non-availability of qualified United States flag capacity to meet national defense requirements, may waive compliance with those laws to the extent, in the manner, and on the terms the individual, in consultation with the Administrator, acting in that capacity, prescribes.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "in consultation with the Administrator" and the required prior "determination" amount to participation. Both the head of the agency and the Maritime Administrator (acting as Director, National Shipping Authority) are federal officials, so this is purely intra-government coordination. No state, company, expert, or member of the public is brought into the waiver decision, and the section requires no rulemaking, hearing, or right to sue.
fable.s: may waive compliance with those laws to the extent, in the manner, and on the terms the individual, in consultation with the Administrator, acting in that capacity, prescribes

qwen_block.w: The section describes a waiver process where the head of an agency acts "in consultation with the Administrator." Both the head of the agency and the Maritime Administrator are federal officials within the executive branch. According to the definition, consultation or coordination between federal agencies or federal officials is intra-government coordination and does not constitute participation by parties outside the federal government.
qwen_block.s: in consultation with the Administrator, acting in that capacity

opus.w: The only consultation is between the head of a federal agency and the Maritime Administrator, who are both federal officials. That is coordination inside the government, not participation. The section does not involve any outside party, such as states, industry or the public, and it provides no comment period, hearing or right to sue. "Prescribes" refers to setting the terms of a particular waiver, not to a rulemaking that the public could comment on.
opus.s: may waive compliance with those laws to the extent, in the manner, and on the terms the individual, in consultation with the Administrator, acting in that capacity, prescribes.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the head of an agency to consult with the Maritime Administrator. Both the head of the agency and the Maritime Administrator are federal officials. The definition explicitly excludes consultation or coordination between federal agencies or federal officials from the definition of participation. Therefore, this is intra-governmental coordination, not participation by outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: in consultation with the Administrator, acting in that capacity, prescribes
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: The phrase "in consultation with the Administrator" suggests participation. However, the "Administrator" refers to the Maritime Administrator, who is a federal official within the Department of Transportation. The definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination *between* federal agencies or federal officials is intra-government coordination and does not count as participation. There are no outside parties (states, tribes, public, companies) involved in this specific consultation requirement.
